Where is Anderson, Indiana, and what is the city like?

Anderson is the county seat of Madison County in east-central Indiana, about 40 miles from Indianapolis. The city covers 41.71 square miles, and the White River crosses its northern part from east to west. Anderson Township holds most of the city, with small pieces of Adams, Fall Creek, Lafayette, Richland and Union townships.

Five ZIP codes serve the city: 46011, 46012, 46013, 46016 and 46017. Several nearby communities, including Country Club Heights, Edgewood, River Forest and Woodlawn Heights, sit outside the city limits, so a house with an Anderson mailing address may not be inside city code enforcement.

Mounds State Park lies along the eastern edge, and the downtown historic district, the Paramount Theatre and Shadyside Memorial Park and Lake are among the landmarks.

How did Anderson's gas boom and factories shape its houses?

Natural gas discovered on March 31, 1887 set off the Indiana gas boom and turned Anderson into a factory town. The city was incorporated in 1865 and became county seat in 1828 after the seat moved from Pendleton. Glassmaking and other gas-fed industries arrived, and the gas ran out in 1912, which sent several plants elsewhere.

Rubber, auto parts and lighting kept the city going. Delco Remy and Guide Lamp, later Fisher Guide, were its top two employers for decades, and about 22,000 people worked for General Motors in Anderson in the 1970s. By 2006 that figure was under 2,600.

The population tells the same story. Anderson peaked at 70,787 in 1970 and counted 54,788 in 2020. Many of the houses were built for the plant workforce of earlier decades, so age and deferred maintenance come up often when owners think about selling.

Who are Anderson's major employers today?

Health care leads the list. As of February 2019, the largest local employers reported by Wikipedia were:

  • Community Hospital Anderson, with 1,980 employees
  • St. Vincent Health, 1,410
  • Nestlé, 790
  • Hoosier Park, 785
  • Carter Express, 680
  • Anderson University, 530
  • Continuum, 500

Kroger, Greenville Technology and Walmart follow with a few hundred each. Those figures are several years old, so treat them as a snapshot. Unemployment has improved but still runs behind the rest of Indiana, according to the same page.

The Church of God has kept its world headquarters in Anderson since 1905, and Anderson University, named in 1988, adds students and staff. Ivy Tech and a Purdue Polytechnic campus are also in the city.

What roads and schools serve Anderson?

State Road 32, which is 14th Street through the center, runs about 19 miles northeast to Muncie and 19 miles southwest to Noblesville. State Road 9, or Scatterfield Road, runs about 11 miles north to Alexandria and 10 miles southwest to Pendleton. Interstate 69 clips the southeast corner at Exit 226, and Fort Wayne is 83 miles away.

Anderson Community School Corporation covers most of the city, with Anderson High School, Highland Middle School, six elementary schools, a kindergarten center and a preschool. A small part of the city falls in South Madison Community School Corporation, and Anderson Preparatory Academy is a tuition-free charter. Check a parcel's district before you tell a buyer which schools apply.

What is Madison County like beyond Anderson?

Madison County covers about 452.9 square miles, nearly all land, and belongs to the Indianapolis-Carmel-Anderson metro area. The legislature authorized it on January 4, 1823 and named it for President James Madison. Pendleton was first chosen as seat, but its off-center spot led to Anderson being platted in 1827.

The terrain is nearly flat, with hillier ground along the White River and Fall Creek, and the high point is a ridgeline in the southeast corner at about 1,010 feet. The 2020 census counted 130,129 residents, down 1.1 percent from 2010, and the median age was 41.5. Besides Anderson, communities include Alexandria, Elwood, Alliance, Emporia and Hamilton.

How does Anderson's climate affect an older house?

Four real seasons, with a hot July and a cold January, test roofs and furnaces. Average annual precipitation is about 46 inches and snowfall about 21 inches, with a July mean high near 84 degrees and a January mean high near 35. The recorded extremes are 105 degrees and minus 24. The page offers a second climate table that gives different averages, so take the numbers as approximate.

Freeze and thaw cycles are hard on older plumbing, masonry and roofs. Those are the repairs a cash buyer weighs when a house is bought as it stands.

What does Anderson code enforcement do?

The city's Department of Municipal Development runs code enforcement and inspections from 120 E. Eighth Street, Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. It administers building codes in existing structures, assesses soundness and habitability, and can require owners to repair a house or remove hazards. If a structure is judged unsafe, occupants must leave.

For emergencies, the city works with public safety departments to board, seal or fence an unsafe structure, and the owner pays those costs. Reports come in by phone at 765-648-6055 or through the Report a Concern tracker on the city website. Vacant and neglected houses draw the most attention, so a seller holding one should resolve open notices before closing.

How are Madison County property taxes paid?

Anderson sits in Madison County, whose spring installment for 2025 taxes was due May 11, 2026. A local news report listed these ways to pay:

  • In person at the Madison County Government Center, Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.
  • By mail to the Treasurer's Office, 16 E. 9th St, Room 109, Anderson, IN 46016, with the original coupon.
  • Online, where an e-check cost $1.95 and a card cost 2.95 percent.
  • By phone at 765-204-9553, with a 95 cent fee.

Indiana caps homestead tax at 1 percent of gross assessed value, other residential at 2 percent and commercial at 3, per the state's Department of Local Government Finance. Appeals begin with Form 130, usually due June 15 for a current-year assessment. Confirm any figure with the county before you rely on it.

What should you settle before selling an Anderson house?

Gather the paperwork that tells a buyer what they are inheriting:

  • The latest tax bill and a payoff for any open installment.
  • Any code enforcement notice or open permit from the city.
  • Proof of who may sign, such as a deed, estate papers or power of attorney.
  • A list of known repairs, such as roof, furnace, plumbing and foundation.

Sellers who list on the open market handle showings and repairs, and those who sell as-is to a cash buyer trade some price for speed and certainty.

More questions about Anderson, IN

Is Anderson, Indiana, in Madison County?

Yes. Anderson is the county seat of Madison County and the county's largest city.

Who handles code enforcement in Anderson?

The Department of Municipal Development, at 120 E. Eighth Street. You can call 765-648-6055 or use the city's Report a Concern tracker.

Where do I pay Madison County property tax?

In person at the Madison County Government Center, by mail to 16 E. 9th St, Room 109, Anderson, online, or by phone. Online and phone payments carry fees.

Can I sell an Anderson house that has code violations?

Yes. Buyers can purchase a house with open issues, but the city may still require repairs or hazard removal, so tell the buyer about every notice and ask the department what is outstanding.

Which school district is Anderson in?

Most of the city is in Anderson Community School Corporation. A small part is in South Madison Community School Corporation, so confirm the address.

Where is Avon, Indiana?

Avon is a town in eastern Hendricks County, Indiana, just west of Indianapolis, and it spreads across Washington and Lincoln townships. Brownsburg borders it on the north, Danville (the county seat) lies to the west, Plainfield to the south, and Marion County to the east.

U.S. Route 36 runs east to west through town. Downtown Indianapolis is about 13 miles away, and Danville is about 7 miles west. The old State Road 267 crossed US 36 in the center of Avon until it was decommissioned in 2013, and that stretch is now Avon Avenue. Avon belongs to the Indianapolis metropolitan area.

How fast has Avon grown?

Avon roughly doubled in the 2000s and grew by nearly three quarters again in the 2010s. It was first settled around 1830, but the town was incorporated only in 1995. A post office opened as Smootsdell in 1868 and was renamed Avon in 1870, after the River Avon in England.

The 2020 census found 7,781 households, 38 percent of them with children under 18, and a median age of 37.4. The town's building office publishes a list of subdivision zoning classifications inside its limits, which helps when you need to know what rules apply to a particular street. Fast growth also means a seller may compare their house with several newer ones nearby, so condition and honest disclosure carry weight in any sale.

What is Hendricks County like?

Hendricks County covers 408.78 square miles and is among the fastest growing counties in Indiana. Danville is the county seat, and Plainfield is the largest town. The General Assembly created the county in December 1823, naming it for Governor William Hendricks, and Danville was chosen as seat in July 1824.

Terrain is low and rolling, with the West and East Forks of White Lick Creek running south. The county grew from 145,448 residents in 2010 to 174,788 in 2020. The 2025 estimate is 193,510, which makes it the third most populous county in the Indianapolis metro area. Avon is one of the incorporated towns on its list, with Brownsburg, Plainfield, Pittsboro and Danville.

Property taxes for an Avon house are billed by Hendricks County, so the treasurer, auditor and assessor there handle the bill, deductions and assessment. Confirm due dates with the county before you rely on any general rule.

Which schools serve Avon?

Most of the town is in Avon Community School Corporation, whose mascot is the Oriole. The district runs Avon High School, three middle schools called North, South and West, eight elementary schools and the White Oak Early Learning Center, and it shares Harris Academy with Brownsburg Community School Corporation. Small parts of Avon fall in the Brownsburg district.

Private options include Kingsway Christian School and Our Shepherd Lutheran School. The Avon-Washington Township Public Library serves the town. The Avon High School marching band is well known: it placed first at the Bands of America Grand Nationals in 2008 and won national titles in 2009, 2010, 2023, 2024 and 2025.

Buyers of a family house often ask which district a parcel sits in, so check the address before you answer.

What does Avon's building department handle?

The Town of Avon's building department handles permits, inspections and zoning at 6570 East US Highway 36, and it is open Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., closed daily from 11:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m. The phone is 317-272-0948.

  • Permit applications listed: building, fence and sign.
  • Inspections are scheduled through a contractor portal that requires an access code.
  • A building permit fee schedule was updated in August 2026, and the page says cashier's checks and credit cards are the accepted payments.
  • Fence standards and sign rules sit in the municipal code.

The page does not mention rental registration or certificates of occupancy, so ask the department directly if either could apply to your house. If you did unpermitted work, such as a deck or a fence, expect questions from a buyer's inspector. An as-is sale lets the buyer take on that cleanup.

How do taxes and caps work for an Avon owner?

An Avon homestead is limited to 1 percent of gross assessed value, according to the state's Department of Local Government Finance, while other residential property is capped at 2 percent and commercial at 3 percent. The auditor applies a credit when the calculated tax is above the cap.

Assessments can be appealed on Form 130, filed with the assessing official, usually by June 15 for a current-year assessment. If the informal meeting fails, the county board must hold a hearing within 180 days, and a further appeal goes to the Indiana Board of Tax Review on Form 131 within 45 days.

The 2025 reform known as SEA 1 phases down the $48,000 standard deduction after 2026 and adds a homestead credit of 10 percent of the bill, up to $300, from 2026, per an analysis in the Indiana Capital Chronicle. That can shift a bill in either direction, so ask the county for the current statement before a closing.

How can an Avon owner follow town decisions that affect property?

The Town of Avon posts agendas, minutes and a document center online, and it lets residents subscribe to alerts on roadwork, events and local news. The Avon Redevelopment Authority and the Redevelopment Commission both had a meeting scheduled for Monday, November 16, 2026, which shows how often public bodies take up land and project items.

The town office is at 6570 East US Highway 36, and its hours match the building department. Because Avon spans two townships and sits beside Marion County, a road project or a new development nearby can change how a buyer sees a street. A seller who wants a quick sale usually wants fewer open questions on the house, and checking these postings is a simple way to know what is coming.

What should an Avon seller check before choosing a sale route?

A seller in a growing town usually has a few buyer options, and the right one depends on condition, timing and cost. Start with these checks:

  • Your homeowners association rules, if the house is in a subdivision with one.
  • Open permits or unpermitted work with the building department.
  • The latest tax bill and any open installment.
  • Whether the mortgage payoff leaves anything after costs.

Listing exposes a house to the widest group of buyers but means showings and negotiation. Selling directly to a cash buyer is faster and carries less risk of a deal falling through.

More questions about Avon, IN

What county is Avon, Indiana in?

Avon is in Hendricks County, whose seat is Danville. The town sits in eastern Hendricks County, west of Indianapolis.

When was Avon incorporated?

Avon was incorporated in 1995, although settlement began around 1830. The population grew from 6,248 in 2000 to 21,474 in 2020.

Where is the Avon building department?

It is at 6570 East US Highway 36, Avon, IN 46123. Call 317-272-0948; hours are Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., with a closing from 11:30 to 12:30.

Which school district serves Avon?

Most of the town is in Avon Community School Corporation. Small parts of Avon fall in the Brownsburg district, so check the specific address.

How long do I have to appeal an Avon property tax assessment?

For a current-year real property assessment, Form 130 is generally due by June 15, depending on when the notice was mailed. File it with the assessing official.
